original_question: For each fixed Delta and all sufficiently large n, if G maximizes the spectral radius among connected nonregular n-vertex graphs with maximum degree Delta, must G have degree sequence (Delta, ..., Delta, delta) where delta equals Delta - 1 when Delta is odd and n is odd, equals 1 when Delta is odd and n is even, and equals Delta - 2 when Delta is even?
target_in_paper: Section 10, "Extreme eigenvalues of nonregular graphs," Conjecture 11 (Liu [103]); this is the modified large-n degree-sequence conjecture for extremal graphs in G(n, Δ).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right extremal setting, the fixed-Δ / sufficiently-large-n regime, and the exact three parity-dependent cases for δ. In particular, the case δ = 1 when Δ is odd and n is even shows that you are aiming at Conjecture 11, not the earlier Liu-Li conjecture immediately above it.
missing_details: The paper uses the notation G(n, Δ) for the class of connected nonregular graphs on n vertices with maximum degree Δ that attain the maximum adjacency spectral radius among all such graphs; your draft states this in words but does not name the class.
The ambient graph model is global in the paper: graphs are simple, undirected, and unweighted.
The spectral quantity is the adjacency spectral radius λ(G) = λ1(G), i.e., the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G); your draft says only "spectral radius."
The conjecture is stated for Δ ≥ 3; your draft says "for each fixed Δ" but does not record this lower bound.

For a stand-alone formulation, "for all sufficiently large n" should be unpacked as: for each fixed Δ there exists N(Δ) such that the claim holds for every n ≥ N(Δ). This dependence on Δ is implicit in the paper.
The degree-sequence notation (Δ, ..., Δ, δ) should be made explicit as meaning exactly n - 1 vertices have degree Δ and exactly one vertex has degree δ.
To stay paper-faithful, the extremality clause should be tied to membership in G(n, Δ), not stated more loosely.
The paper presents this as a modified conjecture motivated by evidence against the earlier two-case Liu-Li conjecture for general Δ; that contextual narrowing is implicit in your draft.
refined_question: Let G(n, Δ) denote the set of connected nonregular simple graphs on n vertices with maximum degree Δ that attain the maximum adjacency spectral radius λ1 among all connected nonregular n-vertex graphs with maximum degree Δ. For each fixed integer Δ ≥ 3, does there exist N(Δ) such that for every n ≥ N(Δ) and every G ∈ G(n, Δ), the degree sequence of G is (Δ, ..., Δ, δ)—that is, exactly n - 1 vertices have degree Δ and one vertex has degree δ—where δ = Δ - 1 if Δ and n are both odd, δ = 1 if Δ is odd and n is even, and δ = Δ - 2 if Δ is even?
justification: The draft matches Section 10, Conjecture 11 exactly: the three-case parity split, especially the case δ = 1 when Δ is odd and n is even, is the distinctive feature of Conjecture 11. It is therefore not the earlier Liu-Li conjecture on the same page, which has only the two cases δ = Δ - 1 when nΔ is odd and δ = Δ - 2 when nΔ is even. The nearby context in Section 10 supplies the notation G(n, Δ) and λ(n, Δ), and the paper’s opening notation supplies the underlying graph model and the meaning of λ(G). The sharp stand-alone rewrite is therefore Conjecture 11 with these definitions spelled out explicitly.
